reason: The text explicitly refers to the Hebrew collective as 'הָעָם' (the people/nation) and portrays them with organizational infrastructure beyond family structures—a camp with gates, tribal divisions (בְנֵי לֵוִי), and hierarchical command structures. The passage describes coordinated national-scale action with thousands involved (כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֖י אִֽישׁ - 'three thousand men'), demonstrating political and military organization characteristic of a nation-state. While the action is framed as obedience to Yahweh, the text foregrounds the Hebrews' existence as an organized people with internal structure, camps, gates, and tribal distinctions—clearly portraying them as more than simply a family unit or passive religious community.
